title: Donor Plants, Explants and Culture Establishment

content.overview: Culture establishment starts before an explant reaches the vessel. Donor health, developmental position, explant age and genotype influence contamination, survival and later multiplication response.

vocabulary.definition: Plant tissue introduced into in-vitro culture.
The early culture phase in which disinfected explants survive and begin stable in-vitro growth.
Poor or inconsistent response of a genotype or tissue to an in-vitro regeneration or propagation protocol.

sections.title: Donor quality affects the starting material
sections.body: Stressed or symptomatic donor tissue can carry higher physiological and microbial risk. Source plants should be documented and inspected before explants are collected.

sections.title: Explant choice changes response
sections.body: Cannabis studies show that explant type and developmental state can strongly affect regeneration and multiplication. A protocol that works for one tissue cannot automatically be generalized to another.

sections.title: Genotype is a major experimental factor
sections.body: Recent multi-genotype work found significant genotype-by-medium effects. Establishment and multiplication records should therefore be analyzed by genotype rather than pooled into one universal success rate.

workedExamples: If one cultivar browns while another remains vigorous on the same medium, document the genotype-specific response before assuming operator error.
If nodal explants survive but hypocotyl explants regenerate more shoots, the two tissues may support different production goals.
commonMistakes: Selecting donor material only by convenience.
Assuming surface disinfection removes internal contaminants.
Pooling all cultivar responses into one protocol average.
content.practicalApplication: Create an establishment log with donor ID, donor condition, explant type and position, disinfection sequence, genotype, medium, survival, contamination and early growth response.
content.summary: Successful establishment is a controlled comparison of donor quality, explant biology, sanitation and genotype response—not simply placing plant tissue into sterile medium.
